replaces: Lesson 9 placeholder seeded in Slice E

intro.title: Business Foundation Blueprint
intro.lead: Every decision you made in this module, on one page, with an honest label on each one. Then three things you'll do in the next 30 days.
intro.quote: You don't graduate because every answer sounds confident. You graduate because you can explain your decisions and name what you still need to learn.
notes: Nothing here is new work. Your answers from Lessons 2 to 8 are quoted back to you. Your job is to read each one and decide: keep it, revise it, or park it.
Unknown is a legal answer. An unknown you've written down is a research priority. An unknown you've papered over is a problem you'll meet in Module 2.
Already running a business? Compare each decision with what's live on your site today and mark what to keep, improve, remove, or test.

callbacks.heading: 1. Business direction
callbacks.template: I am exploring a business that helps {person} solve {problem} through {solution}.

callbacks.heading: 2. The buyer
callbacks.template: She's dealing with {situation}, wants {result}, and is worried about {barrier}.

callback_layout: Each numbered callback is followed immediately by its matching verdict and evidence fields from section 1 (dec_{n}, ev_{n}, note_{n}). Render as one card per decision: the quote on top, the controls beneath.

verdict_options.label: Keep
verdict_options.guide: I'd make the same call today.

verdict_options.label: Revise
verdict_options.guide: Mostly right. Say what changes in the note.

verdict_options.label: Park
verdict_options.guide: Not ready to decide. Say what I need to learn first.

evidence_options.label: Established
evidence_options.guide: Real people said or did this. More than once.

evidence_options.label: Promising, untested
evidence_options.guide: Good reasons to think so. No test yet.

evidence_options.label: Unknown
evidence_options.guide: I haven't checked. This is a research priority, not a failure.

sections.title: Your six decisions
sections.ask: Read each one out loud. Could a stranger understand it? Would you make the same call today?
sections.guide: Each decision depends on the one before it. If you revise the buyer, look again at the problem. If you revise the offer, look again at the blog pathway. That isn't failure. That's a connected strategy.

fields.label: If revised or parked: what changes, or what I need to learn
If revised or parked. Did your Lesson 4 test happen? What did it show?
If revised or parked. Does the headline promise more than you can prove?
If revised or parked. Is there a working link at every step?

sections.footer: A blueprint with two Unknowns and four Keeps is a real plan. A blueprint with six Keeps and no evidence is a wish.

sections.title: If you already have a business
sections.ask: Compare the blueprint with what's live today.
sections.guide: Skip this if you're building from scratch. Otherwise, one line each: what to keep, what to improve, what to remove, what to test. Don't rebuild a working thing because a new template looks prettier.

sections.title: Your next 30 days
sections.ask: Three actions. Not "work on my brand."
sections.guide: One that reduces your biggest unknown (look at your Unknowns above; that's the list). One that makes the buyer's experience better. One that gets you ready for Module 2. Each one has a date and a way to know it's done. If you have five hours a week, this is a five-hour plan.

fields.label: Reduce the biggest unknown
fields.placeholder: e.g. Ask five people from my evidence log the week-two question

fields.label: Done when
fields.placeholder: e.g. Five answers written into my Lesson 3 log

fields.label: Improve the buyer's experience
fields.placeholder: e.g. Rewrite my homepage headline to the Lesson 7 version

fields.label: Get ready for Module 2
fields.placeholder: e.g. Collect the five phrases from my snapshot into one note for the brand work

fields.label: Hours I actually have per week

sections.title: Where you started
sections.ask: Read your Lesson 1 answers. Then write the business in one sentence.
sections.guide: This is the whole point of the module. Compare the person who wrote those answers with the one reading them now.

callbacks_inline.heading: What you'd been treating as your business
What you wanted someone to pay you for

fields.label: My business, in one sentence
fields.template: I help {person} get {result} through {offer}, and my blog brings her to it.

fields.label: What I understand differently now
fields.guide: Two or three sentences. Compare with your Lesson 1 realization.

fields.label: The questions I'm carrying into Module 2
fields.guide: Your Unknowns, in order of how much they'd change if the answer were bad.

fields.label: For coaching: my biggest unresolved decision
fields.guide: Accelerator and Elite members: bring this to your next session. Blueprint members: this is the one to think hardest about.

sections.footer: You came in thinking you needed to do more blogging. You're leaving with a picture of the business your blog is supposed to support. That's the foundation. Module 2 builds on it.

completion.milestone_label: I finished my Business Foundation Blueprint

footer_note: This is your Module 1 blueprint. Module 2 opens with it.

example_response.label: Hypothetical example shown to students as a worked sample. Not a real person.
example_response.note_2: Narrowed from "parents of picky eaters" to parents of picky eaters under six. Every conversation was about a preschooler.
example_response.note_3: Asked five people the week-two question. Four abandoned the plan in week two because it didn't bend around the kid. Not yet a purchase, so promising, not established.
example_response.note_5: Headline promises "dinner decided before 5". I haven't shown it to anyone yet. Testing it in Module 2.
example_response.note_6: No freebie exists yet, so the pathway is a drawing. Build the five-food reset checklist first.
example_response.act_1: Show the headline and the one-sentence promise to the five parents in my log and ask what they think it means.
example_response.act_1_done: Five answers in my Lesson 3 log, with their words
example_response.act_2: Write the five-food weekly reset checklist as a one-page PDF so the pathway has a real freebie.
example_response.act_2_done: PDF exists and two parents have used it for a week
example_response.act_3: Pull the twelve phrases from my snapshot and objections into one note for the brand work.
example_response.act_3_done: Note saved in my Module 2 folder

business_sentence.person: parents of picky eaters under six
business_sentence.result: dinner decided before 5pm without a fight

example_response.changed: In Lesson 1 I wrote that my business was my blog and my Pinterest numbers. It's a kit for one specific parent, and the blog is how she finds it. I also stopped thinking "more recipes" was the product. The product is fewer decisions.
example_response.open_questions: Will she pay monthly or once? Does the partner cook at all? Does the headline mean to her what it means to me?
example_response.coaching_question: Whether to build the kit as a one-time PDF or a monthly membership before I've sold either.
